# Placetta license guides (full text)

Updated 2026-10-17. Source: https://placetta.com/guides/. General information, not legal advice; check each agency's page before filing.

## Answers
### How do I get an EIN without an SSN or ITIN?
File Form SS-4 by fax or mail, or call the IRS international line; applying online needs an SSN or ITIN. On line 7b, a responsible party with neither writes "Foreign". By fax it takes about 4 business days, by mail about 4 to 5 weeks. The IRS charges nothing; sites that charge for an EIN are resellers. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/get-an-ein-without-an-ssn.html

### How long does it take to get an EIN?
With an SSN or ITIN, online, it's issued right away. Without one: about 4 business days by fax, about 4 to 5 weeks by mail, and on the call if you phone the IRS international line. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/how-long-does-an-ein-take.html

### Does a foreign-owned single-member LLC have to file Form 5472?
Yes, every year, attached to a pro forma Form 1120 by the tax return due date. It can't be filed electronically for a disregarded entity, and the penalty for not filing starts at $25,000. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/form-5472-foreign-owned-llc.html

### Do I still need to file a beneficial ownership report (BOIR)?
Only if the company was formed outside the US and registered to do business in a US state. Since March 2025, US-formed companies are exempt. It's free, filed online, and due 30 days after the state registration takes effect. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/do-i-need-to-file-a-boir.html

### How do I become an importer of record in the US?
Get an EIN, create your importer identity with CBP Form 5106 (usually through your customs broker), buy a customs bond (CBP Form 301) from a CBP-approved surety, and open an ACE portal account to see your entries, duties and bond. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/become-an-importer-of-record.html

### Does my business need FDA food facility registration?
Yes if it makes, packs or holds food for US consumption, including facilities abroad. Restaurants and retail food stores are exempt. It's free, filed online, and renewed between October 1 and December 31 of every even-numbered year. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/fda-food-facility-registration.html

### Do I need to register cosmetics with the FDA?
Under MoCRA, the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics registers it (Form FDA 5066, every two years), and the brand on the label lists each product (Form FDA 5067, updated every year). Both are free and filed in Cosmetics Direct. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/register-cosmetics-with-the-fda.html

### Do imported consumer products need a certificate of conformity?
Yes, for products covered by CPSC rules. The importer issues the certificate itself; there is no government form. Under the eFiling rule, the certificate data is filed with CBP at entry. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/certificate-of-conformity-for-imports.html

### How much do permits cost to open a restaurant in New York City?
Across the 10 filings a restaurant in New York City makes, the fixed government fees add up to about $554.60; 3 more depend on the space or business and 3 are free. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/nyc-restaurant-permit-cost.html

### How much do permits cost to open a restaurant in Los Angeles?
Across the 9 filings a restaurant in Los Angeles makes, the fixed government fees add up to about $870; 4 more depend on the space or business and 3 are free. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/los-angeles-restaurant-permit-cost.html

### How much do permits cost to open a restaurant in Houston?
Across the 12 filings a restaurant in Houston makes, the fixed government fees add up to about $325; 6 more depend on the space or business and 4 are free. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/houston-restaurant-permit-cost.html

### Who needs a Food Protection Certificate in New York City?
Every food service establishment: a certified supervisor must be on site whenever you're open. The course is free online; the exam is taken in person. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/nyc-food-protection-certificate.html

### Do I need a seller's permit in California?
Yes, before your first sale, with one permit for each location. Registration is online and free, though CDTFA may ask for a security deposit. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/california-sellers-permit.html

### When do I need a sales tax Certificate of Authority in New York?
Apply through New York Business Express at least 20 days before your first sale. It's free, usually takes about two weeks, and the certificate is displayed at each location. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/new-york-certificate-of-authority.html

### Does a foreign company need to register for VAT in the UK?
Yes, from its first UK sale: a business not established in the UK has no threshold. UK-established businesses register once taxable turnover passes £90,000 in 12 months. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/uk-vat-for-foreign-companies.html

### How do I register a food business in the UK?
Register with your local council at least 28 days before opening. It's free; the council inspects and gives a food hygiene rating. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/uk-food-business-registration.html

### How do I get a trade licence in Dubai?
For a mainland business, reserve the trade name, get initial approval, then issue the licence online through Invest in Dubai. Free zone companies license through their own free zone authority instead. It renews every year. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/dubai-trade-licence.html

### Does a foreign company need a MISA license in Saudi Arabia?
Yes. A foreign-owned business gets the investment license from the Ministry of Investment before its commercial registration, and renews it with the commercial registration. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/saudi-arabia-misa-license.html

### How does a foreign company open a business in China?
Register with the local Administration for Market Regulation on the city's one-stop portal, which also sets up tax, social insurance and the company seal. The foreign investment information report goes through the same registration, and the foreign shareholder's documents need notarization and legalization or an apostille. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/open-a-company-in-china-as-a-foreigner.html

### Do I need a food business license in China?
Yes to make or serve food: apply online after the business license, with the floor plan, equipment list and food safety manager. Selling only prepackaged food needs a filing instead. The license is valid for 5 years. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/china-food-business-license.html

### Does a new California LLC have to pay the $800 tax in its first year?
Yes. Every LLC whose articles are accepted in California, or that does business there, owes the $800 annual tax from its first taxable year, which starts when the Secretary of State files the articles. Pay it with Form FTB 3522 by the 15th day of the 4th month of that year, then every year after. An LLC formed in another state that registers or starts business in California after that date pays right away. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/california-llc-800-tax-first-year.html

### Does a Texas LLC have to file a franchise tax report if it owes no tax?
Yes. Franchise tax applies to every taxable entity formed in Texas or doing business there, and reports are due May 15 each year. Since the 2024 report year there is no No Tax Due Report: an entity with annualized total revenue at or below the no tax due threshold ($2,650,000 for 2026 and 2027 reports) owes nothing but still files a Public Information Report or an Ownership Information Report. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/texas-franchise-tax-no-tax-due.html

### Do I need a sales tax permit in Texas?
Yes if you are engaged in business in Texas and sell, lease or rent taxable goods or provide taxable services. Apply online before your first sale, with one permit for each location. It's free, though the Comptroller may require a security; the permit arrives in about 2 to 3 weeks and doesn't expire. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/texas-sales-tax-permit.html

### How do I get a restaurant permit in New York City?
Apply for the Health Department's Food Service Establishment Permit online, or in person by appointment; new applications aren't accepted by mail. It costs $280, you need a Food Protection Certificate holder or a course registration when you apply, and you may open 22 days after applying, even before the pre-permit inspection. It renews every year. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/nyc-food-service-establishment-permit.html

### How much does a US customs bond cost?
CBP charges nothing for the bond itself (CBP Form 301); you pay a premium to a CBP-approved surety, usually arranged by your customs broker. A continuous bond covers a year of entries with at least $50,000 of coverage and renews yearly. CBP takes at least 5 business days to review it. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/how-much-does-a-customs-bond-cost.html

### Can a Chinese investor get an E-2 visa?
Not as a citizen of the People's Republic of China: the State Department's list of E-1 and E-2 treaty countries doesn't include mainland China or Hong Kong. Taiwan is on the list, as China (Taiwan), for both E-1 and E-2. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/is-china-an-e2-treaty-country.html

### How does a foreign owner get an ITIN?
File Form W-7 with the IRS, generally attached to a US federal tax return unless an exception applies. Mail it with original or certified identity documents, use a Certifying Acceptance Agent, or book an IRS Taxpayer Assistance Center. Allow 7 weeks to hear back. A company doesn't need its owner's ITIN to get an EIN: Form SS-4 works without one. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/how-to-get-an-itin.html

### Does a Chinese company need a US attorney to file a trademark?
Yes. The USPTO requires every applicant domiciled outside the US to be represented by a US-licensed attorney, and every applicant must give and keep current its domicile address. The base application fee is $350 for each class of goods or services. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/us-trademark-for-chinese-companies.html

### Do food shipments from China need FDA Prior Notice?
Yes. Every imported food shipment needs Prior Notice before it arrives: at least 2 hours ahead by road, 4 by rail or air and 8 by water, and before it is sent by international mail. Anyone with the information can submit it, through FDA's system or the customs broker's ABI. Food without proper notice can be refused and held at the port, and food from an unregistered foreign facility can be held until it registers. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/fda-prior-notice-for-food-imports.html

### Is the $800 de minimis exemption still available for imports?
No. Duty-free de minimis ended for goods from China and Hong Kong on May 2, 2025 and for all countries on August 29, 2025. CBP suspended it indefinitely in its regulations on June 24, 2026, so low-value shipments now go through informal or formal entry and pay duty. By law the exemption ends permanently on July 1, 2027. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/de-minimis-800-exemption-status.html

### Does a single-member LLC with no employees need an EIN?
Not for federal tax alone: with no employees and no excise tax, it can use the owner's number. The IRS says most new single-member LLCs still need one, for example to open a bank account or when state tax law requires it. A foreign owner can't apply online and uses Form SS-4 by fax or mail, or the IRS international line. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/does-a-single-member-llc-need-an-ein.html

### Do restaurant workers in California need a food handler card?
Yes. Food workers who prepare, store or handle food must get a California Food Handler Card within 30 days of being hired, from an ANSI-accredited course. The card is valid for three years. Workers who hold a valid food safety certification are exempt. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/california-food-handler-card.html

### Can a foreigner form an LLC in Texas?
Yes. Texas law doesn't restrict who can form or own a business entity, so you don't need to be a US citizen or resident; the organizer only has to be a person capable of entering into a contract. The LLC files Form 205 with the Secretary of State. https://placetta.com/guides/answers/can-a-foreigner-form-a-texas-llc.html

## City guides
### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in New York City
https://placetta.com/guides/new-york-city/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Articles of Organization (New York LLC), New York Department of State, Division of Corporations. Filed online with the Department of State, or mailed. Fee: $200. https://dos.ny.gov/limited-liability-company-articles-organization
3. LLC publication within 120 days, New York Department of State, Division of Corporations. Publish a notice in two newspapers chosen by the county clerk for six weeks, then file the certificate with the affidavits. Fee: $50. https://dos.ny.gov/certificate-publication-domestic-limited-liability-company-0
4. Certificate of Occupancy for the use, NYC Department of Buildings. Check the space's existing CO allows your use; a change of use needs an alteration filing and an amended CO. Fee: Varies. https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/certificate-of-occupancy.page
5. Application for Registration as a Sales Tax Vendor (Certificate of Authority), New York State Department of Taxation and Finance. Apply online through New York Business Express at least 20 days before your first sale. Display the certificate at each location. Fee: Free. https://www.businessexpress.ny.gov/
6. New employer registration for unemployment insurance and withholding, New York State Department of Labor. Register online once you pay wages in New York. Fee: Free. https://dol.ny.gov/register-unemployment-insurance-0
7. Proof of workers' comp and disability/paid family leave insurance, New York State Workers' Compensation Board. Buy the policies from an insurer; the insurer reports coverage to the Board. Agencies ask for the certificates. Fee: Varies. https://www.wcb.ny.gov/content/main/coverage-requirements.jsp
8. Food Protection Certificate (course and exam), NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene. Free online course, then an in-person exam. A certified supervisor must be on site whenever you are open. Fee: $24.60. https://www.nyc.gov/site/doh/business/health-academy/food-protection-online-free.page
9. Food Service Establishment Permit, NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene. Apply on NYC Business. The Health Department inspects before issuing; letter grades follow. Fee: $280. https://nyc-business.nyc.gov/nycbusiness/description/food-service-establishment-permit
10. Sign permit, NYC Department of Buildings. Filed in DOB NOW by a registered design professional or licensed sign hanger. Fee: Varies. https://www.nyc.gov/site/buildings/property-or-business-owner/sign-permit.page

10. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling

7. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/

9. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf

8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
11. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/
12. Packaging producer registration (EPR), CalRecycle, through Circular Action Alliance. The brand owner or importer of packaged goods sold in California registers and reports with the producer organization. Fee: Varies. https://circularactionalliance.org/california
13. Proposition 65 warning labels, California Office of Environmental Health Hazard Assessment. Nothing is filed. Businesses with 10 or more employees warn before exposing Californians to listed chemicals, including online at checkout. Fee: Free. https://www.p65warnings.ca.gov/business-resources/frequently-asked-questions-businesses

3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certified food manager, Texas Department of State Health Services. At least one manager passes an exam from a DSHS-licensed certified food manager program. Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Food establishment plan review, Houston Health Department. Submit plans before building or remodeling a food establishment. Fee: Varies. https://www.houstonhealth.org/food-permits/opening-food-establishment
8. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Houston, Houston Permitting Center. Form CE-1045-A, emailed to Occupancy Inspections (Occupancy.Inspections@houstontx.gov); iPermits is only for paying afterwards. Needed for a new tenant use or change of use inside city limits. Fee: Varies. https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/hpwcode1106
9. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
10. Food dealer permit, Houston Health Department. The operating permit, issued after plan review and inspection. The application is emailed to Food-COO@houstontx.gov. Fee: Varies. https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/hhd1003
11. Sign permit, City of Houston, Sign Administration. Filed with the Houston Permitting Center before the sign goes up. Fee: Varies. https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/hpwcode1112
12. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certified food manager, Texas Department of State Health Services. At least one manager passes an exam from a DSHS-licensed certified food manager program. Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Food establishment plan review, Houston Health Department. Submit plans before building or remodeling a food establishment. Fee: Varies. https://www.houstonhealth.org/food-permits/opening-food-establishment
8. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Houston, Houston Permitting Center. Form CE-1045-A, emailed to Occupancy Inspections (Occupancy.Inspections@houstontx.gov); iPermits is only for paying afterwards. Needed for a new tenant use or change of use inside city limits. Fee: Varies. https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/hpwcode1106
9. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
10. Food dealer permit, Houston Health Department. The operating permit, issued after plan review and inspection. The application is emailed to Food-COO@houstontx.gov. Fee: Varies. https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/hhd1003
11. Sign permit, City of Houston, Sign Administration. Filed with the Houston Permitting Center before the sign goes up. Fee: Varies. https://www.houstonpermittingcenter.org/hpwcode1112
12. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Houston, Houston Permitting Center. Form CE-1045-A, emailed to Occupancy Inspections (Occupancy.Inspections@houstontx.gov); iPermits is only for paying afterwards. Needed for a new tenant use or change of use inside city limits. ### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Beijing
https://placetta.com/guides/beijing/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Company registration and business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation (under SAMR). Filed online on the city's one-stop business portal, which also registers tax, social insurance and the company seal in the same application. Fee: Free. https://www.samr.gov.cn
2. Open the business on Beijing's one-stop portal, Beijing e-Window (e窗通). Beijing's portal takes the company registration, seal, tax, social insurance and invoices in one online application, and is where the food business license is applied for. Fee: Free. https://ect.scjgj.beijing.gov.cn
3. Tax setup and invoicing (new taxpayer), State Taxation Administration. After the license, confirm the tax details, choose the taxpayer type and apply for digital invoices on the province's electronic tax bureau. Fee: Free. https://www.chinatax.gov.cn
4. Employer social insurance and housing fund, Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Housing Provident Fund Center. Employer registration comes with the business license. Enroll each employee within 30 days of hiring and open the housing fund account. Fee: Free. https://www.mohrss.gov.cn
5. Food business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation. Applied for online after the business license, with the floor plan, equipment list and food safety manager. Selling only prepackaged food needs a filing instead of a license. Fee: Free. https://www.samr.gov.cn
6. Fire safety check before opening, Fire and Rescue Department. Shops and restaurants open to the public apply before opening, usually by signing a commitment online; the fire department may inspect afterwards. Fee: Free. https://www.119.gov.cn

2. Open the business on Beijing's one-stop portal, Beijing e-Window (e窗通). Beijing's portal takes the company registration, seal, tax, social insurance and invoices in one online application, and is where the food business license is applied for. Fee: Free. https://ect.scjgj.beijing.gov.cn
3. Tax setup and invoicing (new taxpayer), State Taxation Administration. After the license, confirm the tax details, choose the taxpayer type and apply for digital invoices on the province's electronic tax bureau. Fee: Free. https://www.chinatax.gov.cn
4. Employer social insurance and housing fund, Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Housing Provident Fund Center. Employer registration comes with the business license. Enroll each employee within 30 days of hiring and open the housing fund account. Fee: Free. https://www.mohrss.gov.cn
5. Fire safety check before opening, Fire and Rescue Department. Shops and restaurants open to the public apply before opening, usually by signing a commitment online; the fire department may inspect afterwards. Fee: Free. https://www.119.gov.cn

5. Food business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation. Applied for online after the business license, with the floor plan, equipment list and food safety manager. Selling only prepackaged food needs a filing instead of a license. Fee: Free. https://www.samr.gov.cn
6. Fire safety check before opening, Fire and Rescue Department. Shops and restaurants open to the public apply before opening, usually by signing a commitment online; the fire department may inspect afterwards. Fee: Free. https://www.119.gov.cn

5. Customs registration for importers and exporters, General Administration of Customs. Filed online through the China International Trade Single Window. The separate foreign trade operator filing was abolished in 2022. Fee: Free. https://www.singlewindow.cn

6. Fire safety check before opening, Fire and Rescue Department. Shops and restaurants open to the public apply before opening, usually by signing a commitment online; the fire department may inspect afterwards. Fee: Free. https://www.119.gov.cn

2. Open the business on Wuhan's one-stop portal, Hubei Government Services. Wuhan's portal takes the company registration, seal, tax, social insurance and invoices in one online application, and is where the food business license is applied for. Fee: Free. https://zwfw.hubei.gov.cn

5. Food business license, Local Administration for Market Regulation. Applied for online after the business license, with the floor plan, equipment list and food safety manager. Selling only prepackaged food needs a filing instead of a license. Fee: Free. https://www.samr.gov.cn

6. Fire safety check before opening, Fire and Rescue Department. Shops and restaurants open to the public apply before opening, usually by signing a commitment online; the fire department may inspect afterwards. Fee: Free. https://www.119.gov.cn

2. Open the business on Tianjin's one-stop portal, Tianjin Government Services. Tianjin's portal takes the company registration, seal, tax, social insurance and invoices in one online application, and is where the food business license is applied for. Fee: Free. https://zwfw.tj.gov.cn
3. Tax setup and invoicing (new taxpayer), State Taxation Administration. After the license, confirm the tax details, choose the taxpayer type and apply for digital invoices on the province's electronic tax bureau. Fee: Free. https://www.chinatax.gov.cn
4. Employer social insurance and housing fund, Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; Housing Provident Fund Center. Employer registration comes with the business license. Enroll each employee within 30 days of hiring and open the housing fund account. Fee: Free. https://www.mohrss.gov.cn
5. Customs registration for importers and exporters, General Administration of Customs. Filed online through the China International Trade Single Window. The separate foreign trade operator filing was abolished in 2022. Fee: Free. https://www.singlewindow.cn
6. Fire safety check before opening, Fire and Rescue Department. Shops and restaurants open to the public apply before opening, usually by signing a commitment online; the fire department may inspect afterwards. Fee: Free. https://www.119.gov.cn

5. Premises licence (alcohol or late-night hot food), Local council licensing. Needed only to sell alcohol, or hot food and drink between 11pm and 5am. Fee: Varies. https://www.gov.uk/premises-licence

2. VAT registration, HM Revenue & Customs. Required once taxable turnover passes £90,000 in 12 months. A business not established in the UK registers from its first UK sale. Fee: Free. https://www.gov.uk/register-for-vat
3. Employer registration (PAYE), HM Revenue & Customs. Register before the first payday; it can take up to 5 working days to get the employer reference. Fee: Free. https://www.gov.uk/register-employer
4. EORI number for importing, HM Revenue & Customs. Needed before moving goods into the UK. Fee: Free. https://www.gov.uk/eori

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Berlin
https://placetta.com/guides/berlin/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Commercial register entry (GmbH), Local court (Registergericht), through a notary. The articles are notarized and the notary files the registration electronically. Fee: Varies. https://www.handelsregister.de
2. Transparency register (beneficial owners), Bundesanzeiger Verlag, Transparency Register. Companies record their beneficial owners online. Fee: Varies. https://www.transparenzregister.de
3. Trade registration, Bezirksamt Berlin, Ordnungsamt. Every shop, restaurant and trading business registers its trade with Berlin before starting. The city passes it on to the tax office and the food inspectors. Fee: Varies. https://service.berlin.de/dienstleistung/121921/
4. Tax registration questionnaire, Finanzamt (through ELSTER). Filed online through ELSTER within a month of starting; the tax office then issues the tax number and VAT ID. Fee: Free. https://www.elster.de

1. Commercial register entry (GmbH), Local court (Registergericht), through a notary. The articles are notarized and the notary files the registration electronically. Fee: Varies. https://www.handelsregister.de
2. Transparency register (beneficial owners), Bundesanzeiger Verlag, Transparency Register. Companies record their beneficial owners online. Fee: Varies. https://www.transparenzregister.de
3. Trade registration, Bezirksamt Berlin, Ordnungsamt. Every shop, restaurant and trading business registers its trade with Berlin before starting. The city passes it on to the tax office and the food inspectors. Fee: Varies. https://service.berlin.de/dienstleistung/121921/
4. Tax registration questionnaire, Finanzamt (through ELSTER). Filed online through ELSTER within a month of starting; the tax office then issues the tax number and VAT ID. Fee: Free. https://www.elster.de

1. Commercial register entry (GmbH), Local court (Registergericht), through a notary. The articles are notarized and the notary files the registration electronically. Fee: Varies. https://www.handelsregister.de
2. Transparency register (beneficial owners), Bundesanzeiger Verlag, Transparency Register. Companies record their beneficial owners online. Fee: Varies. https://www.transparenzregister.de
3. Trade registration, Stadt Frankfurt am Main, Ordnungsamt. Every shop, restaurant and trading business registers its trade with Frankfurt before starting. The city passes it on to the tax office and the food inspectors. Fee: Varies. https://frankfurt.de
4. Tax registration questionnaire, Finanzamt (through ELSTER). Filed online through ELSTER within a month of starting; the tax office then issues the tax number and VAT ID. Fee: Free. https://www.elster.de

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Madrid
https://placetta.com/guides/madrid/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Company creation (CIRCE), Ministerio de Economía, CIRCE / PAE. A limited company (SL) can be created online through CIRCE with the single electronic document. Fee: Varies. https://paeelectronico.es
2. Tax census declaration, Agencia Tributaria. Registers the business for VAT and income tax before it starts trading. Fee: Free. https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
3. Employer registration with Social Security, Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social. Register as an employer and sign up each worker before they start. Fee: Free. https://sede.seg-social.gob.es
4. Opening licence or responsible declaration, Ayuntamiento de Madrid. Most shops and restaurants open with a responsible declaration filed online; larger works need a licence. Fee: Varies. https://sede.madrid.es

4. Food establishment approval, Dubai Municipality, Food Safety. Food businesses get the municipality's layout approval and inspection before the licence is activated. Fee: Varies. https://www.dm.gov.ae

1. Dubai trade licence, Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism. Reserve the trade name, get initial approval, then issue the licence online through Invest in Dubai. Free zones license through their own authority instead. Fee: Varies. https://invest.dubai.ae
2. Corporate tax and VAT registration, Federal Tax Authority. Every company registers for corporate tax on EmaraTax. VAT registration is required once taxable supplies pass AED 375,000 a year. Fee: Free. https://eservices.tax.gov.ae
3. Employer registration and work permits, Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. Register the establishment, then apply for each employee's work permit. Fee: Varies. https://www.mohre.gov.ae

3. Tax, VAT and zakat registration, Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA). Register for zakat or income tax, and for VAT once taxable supplies pass SAR 375,000 a year. E-invoicing applies. Fee: Free. https://zatca.gov.sa
4. Social insurance employer registration, General Organization for Social Insurance. Register as an employer and enroll each employee. Fee: Free. https://www.gosi.gov.sa

6. Civil Defense safety license, General Directorate of Civil Defense. Premises open to the public and warehouses get the safety license online. Fee: Varies. https://998.gov.sa

2. Commercial registration, Ministry of Commerce, Saudi Business Center. Registered online through the Saudi Business Center. Fee: Varies. https://business.sa
3. Tax, VAT and zakat registration, Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority (ZATCA). Register for zakat or income tax, and for VAT once taxable supplies pass SAR 375,000 a year. E-invoicing applies. Fee: Free. https://zatca.gov.sa
4. Social insurance employer registration, General Organization for Social Insurance. Register as an employer and enroll each employee. Fee: Free. https://www.gosi.gov.sa
5. Municipal license, Ministry of Municipal and Rural Affairs and Housing (Balady). Every shop, restaurant and warehouse gets the municipal license for its premises online. Fee: Varies. https://balady.gov.sa
6. Civil Defense safety license, General Directorate of Civil Defense. Premises open to the public and warehouses get the safety license online. Fee: Varies. https://998.gov.sa

3. Municipal trade licence, Ministry of Municipality. The premises get a municipal trade licence. Fee: Varies. https://www.mm.gov.qa

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in San Francisco
https://placetta.com/guides/san-francisco/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Articles of Organization (California LLC), California Secretary of State. Filed online in bizfile Online. Fee: $70. https://bizfileonline.sos.ca.gov/
3. Seller's permit, California Department of Tax and Fee Administration. Register online before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://onlineservices.cdtfa.ca.gov/
4. San Francisco Business Registration Certificate, San Francisco Office of the Treasurer and Tax Collector. Apply online, sign the DocuSign email within 15 days, then pay the fee when asked. Fee: $55. https://etaxstatement.sfgov.org/NewBusinessRegistration/application
5. Formula retail (chain store) affidavit, San Francisco Planning Department. A chain with 11 or more other locations worldwide files this with the building permit. Many neighborhood districts then require a Conditional Use hearing, and a few ban chains. Fee: Varies. https://sfplanning.org/resource/formula-retail-establishments
6. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/
7. Food facility plan check, San Francisco Department of Public Health. Filed with the building permit at the Permit Center, with health as a review station: the application, plans and the review fee. Fee: $2,207. https://sf.gov/sites/default/files/2023-07/PlanCheckApplication.pdf
8. Building permit for a tenant improvement, San Francisco Department of Building Inspection. Submit plans and the application at the Permit Center, which routes it to Planning, Fire and Health. Fee: Varies. https://www.sf.gov/step-by-step--get-otc-permit-your-commercial-project/
9. Health permit to operate a food facility, San Francisco Department of Public Health. Apply online at least six weeks before opening, with your business account, location ID and federal tax ID, once a certified food safety manager is on staff. Fee: $470. https://sf.gov/get-health-permit-open-restaurant-bar-or-other-retail-food-location
10. Sign and awning permit, San Francisco Department of Building Inspection. Online only through PermitSF since June 29, 2026 (Forms 4 and 7 retired): submit drawings, answer plan review, pay, then book the final inspection. Lit signs also need an electrical permit. Fee: Varies. https://sf.gov/step-by-step/get-permit-install-sign-or-awning
11. Fire Department place of assembly permit, San Francisco Fire Department. For dining rooms above the assembly occupant load: file with the Fire Prevention permits section, which inspects before issuing. Fee: $446. https://sf-fire.org/permits
12. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. San Francisco Business Registration Certificate, San Francisco Office of the Treasurer and Tax Collector. Apply online, sign the DocuSign email within 15 days, then pay the fee when asked. Fee: $55. https://etaxstatement.sfgov.org/NewBusinessRegistration/application

Fee: Varies. https://sf.gov/step-by-step/get-permit-install-sign-or-awning
13. LLC annual tax ($800), California Franchise Tax Board. Paid every year by every LLC registered or doing business in California. Fee: $800. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/

Fee: Varies. https://deh.santaclaracounty.gov/food-and-retail/compliance-retail-food-operations/submit-plan-review-restaurants-grocery-stores-and

9. Building final inspection, City of San José Building Division. Schedule the final on SJPermits.org once every other inspection on the permit has passed. Fee: Varies. https://www.sjpermits.org
10. Health permit to operate a food facility, County of Santa Clara Department of Environmental Health. Submit the permit application by email or in person at or before the final inspection; the operating fee is invoiced after the final. 5. Registration Form for Commercial Employers, California Employment Development Department. Register in e-Services for Business within 15 days of paying over $100 in wages. Fee: Free. https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/save_time_and_register_online/

Fee: Varies. https://deh.santaclaracounty.gov/food-and-retail/compliance-retail-food-operations/submit-plan-review-restaurants-grocery-stores-and
7. Building permit for a tenant improvement, City of San José Building Division. Apply on SJPermits.org, upload plans through SJePlans and pay the plan review fee before review starts. Restaurants can use the city's Streamlined Restaurant Program. Fee: Varies. https://www.sjpermits.org

9. Building final inspection, City of San José Building Division. Schedule the final on SJPermits.org once every other inspection on the permit has passed. Fee: Varies. https://www.sjpermits.org

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Boston
https://placetta.com/guides/boston/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. LLC formation, Secretary of the Commonwealth, Corporations Division. Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $500. https://www.sec.state.ma.us
3. Sales tax registration, Massachusetts Department of Revenue. Register for sales tax and withholding before trading. Fee: Free. https://mtc.dor.state.ma.us
4. Certified food protection manager, Massachusetts Department of Public Health, Food Protection Program. At least one manager on staff passes a food protection manager exam from a nationally accredited provider that Massachusetts accepts; a backup person in charge covers when they're away. Boston asks for the certificate with the food service permit application. Fee: Varies. https://www.mass.gov/doc/massachusetts-food-protection-manager-certification-exam-and-trainer-directory-1/download
5. Allergen awareness certificate, Massachusetts Department of Public Health, Food Protection Program. The person in charge, who must be on site whenever the place is open, and the backup who covers for them take an allergen awareness course and train the staff. Places that cook, prepare or serve food to eat right away need it; Boston asks for the certificate before the opening inspection. ### Cosmetics stores in Boston
https://placetta.com/guides/boston/cosmetics-store.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. LLC formation, Secretary of the Commonwealth, Corporations Division. Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $500. https://www.sec.state.ma.us
3. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
4. Sales tax registration, Massachusetts Department of Revenue. Register for sales tax and withholding before trading. Fee: Free. https://mtc.dor.state.ma.us
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Boston business certificate (DBA), City of Boston, City Clerk. Needed when the business trades under a name other than its legal name. Bring the notarized form, the signed lease and photo ID to City Hall, Room 601 (the clerk notarizes free), or mail them with a check; there is no online filing. An LLC or corporation registers with the Secretary of the Commonwealth first. Fee: $65. https://www.boston.gov/sites/default/files/file/2025/03/2025-New-Business-Certificate-Form_0.pdf

A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certified food manager, Texas Department of State Health Services. At least one manager passes an exam from a DSHS-licensed certified food manager program. Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
8. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Dallas Planning and Development. Apply on DallasNow with the land use questionnaire, plus site and floor plans if the use is changing. Needed for a new tenant or a change of use. Fee: $375. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/certificate_occupancy.aspx
9. Building permit for tenant finish-out, City of Dallas Planning and Development. Apply on DallasNow under Commercial Permits, upload the plans and checklists, and pay online. Fee: Varies. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/pages/fees.aspx
10. Food establishment plan review, City of Dallas Planning and Development, Health Plan Review. Submit two sets of plans, equipment sheets, finishes and the menu at 320 E. Jefferson Blvd., where the plans are reviewed and stamped. Fee: $200. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/Health-Inspections.aspx
11. Food establishment permit, City of Dallas Code Compliance, Consumer Health. File CCS-FRM-424 with photo ID, the Texas sales tax permit and the fee, then book the health inspection. A registered food manager must be on site. Fee: $121. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/codecompliance/consumer-health/Pages/food-establishment.aspx
12. Sign permit, City of Dallas Planning and Development. A registered sign contractor applies on DallasNow once the Certificate of Occupancy is approved. Fee: $296. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/Signs.aspx
13. Kitchen hood fire-extinguishing system permit, Dallas Fire-Rescue. Get the application from Dallas Fire-Rescue, 1551 Baylor St., Suite 400. Fee: $250. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/fire-rescue/Pages/Prevention-and-Investigation-Bureau.aspx
14. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Cosmetics stores in Dallas
https://placetta.com/guides/dallas/cosmetics-store.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
11. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Dallas Planning and Development. Apply on DallasNow with the land use questionnaire, plus site and floor plans if the use is changing. Needed for a new tenant or a change of use. Fee: $375. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/certificate_occupancy.aspx
12. Sign permit, City of Dallas Planning and Development. A registered sign contractor applies on DallasNow once the Certificate of Occupancy is approved. Fee: $296. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/Signs.aspx
13. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

8. Hazardous materials registration, Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (DOT). Filed online when you ship or offer certain hazardous materials in bulk, such as large lithium battery shipments. Fee: Varies. https://hazmatonline.phmsa.dot.gov/services/
9. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
10. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Dallas Planning and Development. Apply on DallasNow with the land use questionnaire, plus site and floor plans if the use is changing. Needed for a new tenant or a change of use. Fee: $375. https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/certificate_occupancy.aspx
11. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in Austin
https://placetta.com/guides/austin/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certified food manager, Texas Department of State Health Services. At least one manager passes an exam from a DSHS-licensed certified food manager program. Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
8. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Austin Development Services. Needed when the space's use changes or after construction; it may include a site plan exemption and building plan review. For a food business it comes through Austin Public Health's pre-opening inspection. Fee: Varies. https://www.austintexas.gov/development-services/small-business-permitting
9. Building permit for a tenant finish-out, City of Austin Development Services. Apply with the city's commercial building permit web form (not AB+C) to build, alter or convert the space, with plans for commercial plan review. Fee: Varies. https://austintexas.jotform.com/austin-dsd/commercial-building-permit-web-form
10. Food establishment plan review, City of Austin Development Services, with Austin Public Health. For new construction or a remodel: inside the City of Austin, apply online through Development Services; in unincorporated Travis County, through Austin Public Health's My Health Department portal. Fee: $312. https://www.austintexas.gov/health/programs/fixed-food-establishments
11. Pre-opening health inspection, Austin Public Health, Environmental Health Services. Apply on the My Health Department portal (Retail and Wholesale Food Applications, Pre-Opening Inspection), in person at 1520 Rutherford Ln, or by mail. Needed for a new place, a remodel or a change of owner; the place must pass before the permit is issued. Fee: $178. https://www.austintexas.gov/health/programs/fixed-food-establishments
12. Food enterprise permit (fixed food establishment), Austin Public Health, Environmental Health Services. Issued after the pre-opening inspection passes. Apply on the My Health Department portal (Food Enterprise, Operational Permit Application) or in person at 1520 Rutherford Ln; the form says mailed applications are not accepted. A certified food manager must be on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. https://www.austintexas.gov/health/programs/fixed-food-establishments
13. Sign permit, City of Austin Development Services. Any outdoor sign (wall, awning, projecting, freestanding, roof) needs a permit, applied for on the AB+C portal. Fee: Varies. https://abc.austintexas.gov
14. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

https://placetta.com/guides/austin/cosmetics-store.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
7. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
11. Certificate of Occupancy, City of Austin Development Services. Needed when the space's use changes or after construction; it may include a site plan exemption and building plan review. For a food business it comes through Austin Public Health's pre-opening inspection. Fee: Varies. https://www.austintexas.gov/development-services/small-business-permitting
12. Sign permit, City of Austin Development Services. Any outdoor sign (wall, awning, projecting, freestanding, roof) needs a permit, applied for on the AB+C portal. Fee: Varies. https://abc.austintexas.gov
13. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

2. LLC formation, Georgia Secretary of State, Corporations. Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: Varies. https://ecorp.sos.ga.gov
3. Sales tax registration, Georgia Department of Revenue. Register for sales and withholding tax online. Fee: Free. https://gtc.dor.ga.gov
4. Certified food safety manager, Georgia Department of Public Health, Environmental Health. At least one employee with supervisory and management duties passes an accredited food safety manager exam, and is designated to this one place only. A new food service establishment has 60 days from its permit to employ one, and tells the county within 30 days if it loses its manager. Fee: Varies. https://dph.georgia.gov/node/146
5. Atlanta business license, City of Atlanta, Department of Finance, Office of Revenue. Every business location inside city limits registers. Apply on the city's ATLBiz portal with a government photo ID, the articles of incorporation, notarized SAVE and E-Verify affidavits and the EIN; the city runs the zoning review itself, and some kinds of business also upload a regulatory permit. Fee: Varies. https://atlbiz.atlantaga.gov/_/
6. Food service plan review, Fulton County Board of Health, Environmental Health Services. Before building or extensively remodeling, mail or bring the application, scaled plans, equipment specifications and the fee to the Environmental Health district office nearest the restaurant. An Atlanta address in DeKalb County applies to the DeKalb County Board of Health instead. Fee: Varies. https://FultonCountyGa.gov/-/media/Departments/Board-of-Health/Environmental-Health/Restaurant-Inspection/Link-List-Items/Food-Service-Application.pdf
7. Food service permit, Fulton County Board of Health, Environmental Health Services. Issued by the county once the application and fee are in, the plans are approved and the place passes its pre-opening inspection; apply by mail or in person at the district office nearest the restaurant. An Atlanta address in DeKalb County gets its permit from the DeKalb County Board of Health instead. Fee: Varies. https://fultoncountyga.gov/Inside-Fulton-County/Fulton-County-Departments/Board-of-Health/Environmental-Health/Restaurant-Inspection

A new food service establishment has 60 days from its permit to employ one, and tells the county within 30 days if it loses its manager. Fee: Varies. https://dph.georgia.gov/node/146
5. Atlanta business license, City of Atlanta, Department of Finance, Office of Revenue. Every business location inside city limits registers. Apply on the city's ATLBiz portal with a government photo ID, the articles of incorporation, notarized SAVE and E-Verify affidavits and the EIN; the city runs the zoning review itself, and some kinds of business also upload a regulatory permit. Fee: Varies. https://atlbiz.atlantaga.gov/_/
6. Food service plan review, Fulton County Board of Health, Environmental Health Services. Before building or extensively remodeling, mail or bring the application, scaled plans, equipment specifications and the fee to the Environmental Health district office nearest the restaurant. An Atlanta address in DeKalb County applies to the DeKalb County Board of Health instead. Fee: Varies. https://FultonCountyGa.gov/-/media/Departments/Board-of-Health/Environmental-Health/Restaurant-Inspection/Link-List-Items/Food-Service-Application.pdf
7. Food service permit, Fulton County Board of Health, Environmental Health Services. Issued by the county once the application and fee are in, the plans are approved and the place passes its pre-opening inspection; apply by mail or in person at the district office nearest the restaurant. An Atlanta address in DeKalb County gets its permit from the DeKalb County Board of Health instead. ### Cosmetics stores in Atlanta
https://placetta.com/guides/atlanta/cosmetics-store.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. LLC formation, Georgia Secretary of State, Corporations. Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: Varies. https://ecorp.sos.ga.gov
3. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
4. Sales tax registration, Georgia Department of Revenue. Register for sales and withholding tax online. Fee: Free. https://gtc.dor.ga.gov
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Atlanta business license, City of Atlanta, Department of Finance, Office of Revenue. Every business location inside city limits registers. Apply on the city's ATLBiz portal with a government photo ID, the articles of incorporation, notarized SAVE and E-Verify affidavits and the EIN; the city runs the zoning review itself, and some kinds of business also upload a regulatory permit. Fee: Varies. https://atlbiz.atlantaga.gov/_/

1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. LLC formation, Pennsylvania Department of State. Form the LLC or register a foreign company online. Fee: $125. https://file.dos.pa.gov
3. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
4. Sales tax license, Pennsylvania Department of Revenue. Register for the sales tax license and employer withholding. Fee: Free. https://mypath.pa.gov
5. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf
6. Cosmetic product facility registration (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the facility that makes or processes the cosmetics. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
7. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
8. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
9. Commercial activity license, City of Philadelphia, Department of Licenses and Inspections. Every business in Philadelphia gets the free commercial activity license online; food businesses also get a health license. Fee: Free. https://eclipse.phila.gov

### Milk tea and bubble tea shops in San Antonio
https://placetta.com/guides/san-antonio/milk-tea-shop.html
1. Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN), Internal Revenue Service. Owners with an SSN or ITIN apply online. A company whose responsible party has neither (most China-based owners) faxes or mails Form SS-4, or calls the IRS international line. Fee: Free. https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/fss4.pdf
2. Certificate of Formation (Texas LLC), Texas Secretary of State. Filed online in SOSDirect, or by mail or fax. Fee: $300. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/205_boc.pdf
3. Assumed Name Certificate (DBA), Texas Secretary of State. Filed when the store trades under a name other than the legal name. Fee: $25. https://www.sos.state.tx.us/corp/forms/503_boc.pdf
4. Texas Sales and Use Tax Permit Application, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Apply online in eSystems before your first sale; one permit for each location. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/permit/
5. Certified food manager, Texas Department of State Health Services. At least one manager passes an exam from a DSHS-licensed certified food manager program. Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
8. Certificate of Occupancy, City of San Antonio Development Services. Needed when the new business is a different type of business than the one in the building now; a new owner or tenant with the same use only updates the name on the existing certificate. Expect building, electrical, mechanical, plumbing and fire inspections. Fee: Varies. https://www.sanantonio.gov/DSD/Business/CofO
9. Food establishment license, San Antonio Metropolitan Health District (Metro Health). Once the space is zoned for the use and the Certificate of Occupancy requirements are complete, buy the license at the Development and Business Services Center, 1901 S. Alamo. Fee: Varies. https://www.sanantonio.gov/Health/FoodLicensing/FAQs
10. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

Local health departments require a certified food manager on site whenever the place is open. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-managers
6. Food handler certificates for staff, Texas Department of State Health Services. Every employee who works with unpackaged food, equipment or food-contact surfaces finishes an accredited food handler course within 30 days of hire. Certified food managers are exempt. Fee: Varies. https://www.dshs.texas.gov/food-handlers
7. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax
8. Certificate of Occupancy, City of San Antonio Development Services. Needed when the new business is a different type of business than the one in the building now; a new owner or tenant with the same use only updates the name on the existing certificate. Expect building, electrical, mechanical, plumbing and fire inspections. Fee: Varies. https://www.sanantonio.gov/DSD/Business/CofO
9. Food establishment license, San Antonio Metropolitan Health District (Metro Health). Once the space is zoned for the use and the Certificate of Occupancy requirements are complete, buy the license at the Development and Business Services Center, 1901 S. Alamo. Fee: Varies. https://www.sanantonio.gov/Health/FoodLicensing/FAQs
10. Franchise tax annual report, Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts. Filed every year by May 15, even when no tax is due. Fee: Free. https://comptroller.texas.gov/taxes/franchise/

5. Create/Update Importer Identity Form, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Sent to CBP (usually through your customs broker), or created in the ACE portal. Needed before your first entry as importer of record. Fee: Free. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/cbp_form_5106.pdf
6. Customs Bond, U.S. Customs and Border Protection. Bought from a CBP-approved surety, usually through your customs broker, who files it electronically. A continuous bond covers a year of entries. Fee: Varies. https://www.cbp.gov/sites/default/files/2024-05/cbp_form_301.pdf

8. Cosmetic product listing (MoCRA), U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Filed online in Cosmetics Direct by the brand (the responsible person on the label), one listing per product. Fee: Free. https://www.fda.gov/cosmetics/registration-listing-cosmetic-product-facilities-and-products
9. Product safety certificate, filed electronically at entry, U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The importer issues the certificate itself (there is no government form) and, under the eFiling rule, files the certificate data with CBP at entry. Fee: Free. https://www.cpsc.gov/eFiling
10. Unemployment tax account, Texas Workforce Commission. Register online once you pay wages in Texas. Fee: Free. https://www.twc.texas.gov/services/register-tax

5. City of Tampa business tax receipt, City of Tampa Business Tax. A business inside Tampa city limits files the new business application online; the city may inspect the site. Fee: Varies. https://www.tampa.gov/service/new-business-tax-receipt-application
6. Restaurant license, Florida DBPR, Division of Hotels and Restaurants. Restaurants get the state food service license after plan review and inspection. Fee: Varies. https://www2.myfloridalicense.com
